issue_context.title: Revisit NonBacktracking's avoiding of findOptimizations.LeadingAnchor
issue_context.body:
Today the Regex non-backtracking implementation uses the same RegexFindOptimizations instance as does the interpreter, gaining most of the same "quickly move to the next location to start a match" optimizations.  But it explicitly ignores the optimizations when it has a leading anchor:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/be20c44826bc55d201c406f4ac007d24ed7a9137/src/libraries/System.Text.RegularExpressions/src/System/Text/RegularExpressions/Symbolic/SymbolicRegexMatcher.cs#L194
That's because the DFA/NFA itself has knowledge of the anchors.  But this misses out on various vectorized operations, such as quickly jumping to the next line if there's a beginning-of-line anchor.  We should revisit this to see whether there are ways to better utilize all of the same find optimizations as the other engines.

cc: @olsaarik

I'm guessing that limitation should just be removed. At least it shouldn't be a problem, as `NonBacktracking` sets the new initial state according to the new character context after `RegexFindOptimizations` has jumped ahead. The vectorized search for matching anchor locations would probably be very helpful for some patterns.
I'll try removing it and report back.

review_comments: NIT: should this second check for LeadingAnchor being Beginning be also collapsed to the IsUseful method since this is the only place it gets used?

I'd prefer not to, purely as a layering thing.  It's true that right now nothing else calls this IsUseful, but that property is encoding RegexFindOptimization's details about whether it provides any useful optimizations... then at the NonBacktracking layer, NonBacktracking is special-casing something it knows it can do better for one particular optimization provided.
